subject: pharmacology
title: Pseudocholinesterase Deficiency, Pharmacokinetic Drug Interactions, Pregnancy Categories, and Geriatric Prescribing

steps.tx: The duration of neuromuscular paralysis elicited by the depolarizing agent succinylcholine is normally limited to five to ten minutes because of rapid enzymatic hydrolysis by butyrylcholinesterase synthesized in hepatocytes and circulating in plasma. An inherited autosomal recessive pharmacogenetic defect resulting in atypical plasma butyrylcholinesterase that fails to hydrolyse neuromuscular blockers is designated **pseudocholinesterase deficiency**. Affected individuals exposed to standard intubation doses of succinylcholine or mivacurium experience flaccid paralysis lasting hours.
steps.say: Pseudocholinesterase deficiency is an inherited enzymopathy where atypical plasma cholinesterase fails to hydrolyse succinylcholine, causing prolonged paralysis.

steps.tx: Laboratory diagnosis of atypical butyrylcholinesterase relies on measuring the percentage inhibition of plasma enzyme activity by the local anaesthetic dibucaine, expressed as the **dibucaine number**. Normal plasma cholinesterase is inhibited approximately eighty percent by dibucaine, whereas the homozygous atypical enzyme variant is resistant to dibucaine inhibition and demonstrates a low dibucaine number around twenty. When prolonged post-succinylcholine apnoea occurs, management requires continued mechanical ventilation and sedation until spontaneous muscular recovery ensues.
steps.say: A low dibucaine number of twenty confirms homozygous atypical pseudocholinesterase, managed by continued mechanical ventilation.

left.title: Normal plasma cholinesterase
points: Recovery of spontaneous breathing in 5-10 min

steps.tx: When two or more pharmaceutical agents are co-administered, one drug may alter the magnitude or duration of response to another through complex **drug interactions**. Pharmacokinetic interactions alter absorption, protein binding, metabolism, or renal excretion of a victim drug, altering its systemic bioavailability and plasma half-life. In contrast, pharmacodynamic interactions occur directly at common receptor or physiological effector pathways, yielding additive, synergistic, or antagonistic effects without altering plasma drug concentrations.
steps.say: Drug interactions divide into pharmacokinetic alterations in drug disposition and pharmacodynamic interactions at shared physiological receptors.

Induction of CYP2C9 and CYP3A4 by rifampicin
Rapid clearance of warfarin causing thrombosis
Loss of bronchodilation and severe bronchospasm

steps.tx: Antiepileptic drugs like carbamazepine exemplify potent pharmacokinetic interactions by strongly inducing hepatic microsomal cytochrome P450 enzymes including CYP1A2, CYP2C9, and CYP3A4. Chronic carbamazepine therapy accelerates the hepatic biotransformation and clearance of concurrent medications including oral contraceptives, warfarin, and cyclosporine, often causing unexpected therapeutic failure. Furthermore, carbamazepine exhibits autoinduction, progressively accelerating its own hepatic metabolism over the initial four to six weeks of therapy, requiring systematic **antiepileptic therapeutic monitoring**.
steps.say: Carbamazepine induces multiple cytochrome enzymes, lowering levels of oral contraceptives and warfarin while accelerating its own elimination.

steps.tx: Prescribing during pregnancy requires rigorous evaluation of maternal benefit against potential fetal embryopathy, previously structured by the five-tier **pregnancy category** system established by the United States Food and Drug Administration. While Category A designates medications with rigorous human controlled trials demonstrating no fetal harm, Category X identifies drugs where fetal risks clearly outweigh any conceivable maternal benefit, constituting absolute contraindications during pregnancy. Modern labeling has transitioned to narrative Pregnancy and Lactation Labeling Rule risk summaries.
steps.say: FDA pregnancy categories range from Category A safe drugs to Category X compounds absolutely contraindicated in pregnancy.

steps.tx: Major anatomical birth defects result from fetal exposure to potent teratogenic pharmaceuticals during the critical organogenesis window. Ingestion of the vitamin A analogue isotretinoin causes craniofacial dysmorphism, microtia, and thymic hypoplasia through cranial neural crest disruption. Anticonvulsant exposure to valproate induces spina bifida and neural tube defects, while administration of angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors during the second and third trimesters produces **fetal renal dysgenesis**, profound oligohydramnios, pulmonary hypoplasia, and neonatal anuria.
steps.say: Potent teratogens include isotretinoin causing ear and face anomalies, valproate causing spina bifida, and ACE inhibitors causing renal dysgenesis.

steps.tx: Age-related physiological changes markedly alter drug absorption, distribution, hepatic metabolism, and renal excretion in elderly individuals. Aging is accompanied by reduced total body water, increased relative body fat, decreased circulating plasma albumin, diminished hepatic blood flow, and progressive loss of functional nephrons. These physiological alterations substantially prolong the elimination half-life of lipid-soluble drugs and impair renal clearance, predisposing to drug accumulation and severe **geriatric pharmacokinetic toxicity**.
steps.say: Aging decreases body water, reduces albumin, and diminishes renal glomerular filtration, causing drug accumulation and toxicity.

rows: Marked reduction in renal drug clearance
Enlarged volume of distribution for lipophilic drugs
Prolonged daytime sedation, falls and hip fractures
Acute delirium, cognitive decline, urinary retention

steps.tx: To reduce preventable iatrogenic morbidity and adverse drug events in older adults, clinical practice relies on the evidence-based American Geriatrics Society **Beers Criteria**. The Beers Criteria systematically identify medications where potential hazards generally exceed anticipated clinical benefits in older patients. High-risk classes flagged for avoidance include potent first-generation antihistamines, tertiary tricyclic antidepressants, long-acting benzodiazepines, muscle relaxants, and sliding-scale regular insulin regimens that provoke severe neuroglycopenia.
steps.say: The AGS Beers Criteria identify inappropriate medications in elderly patients to prevent falls, anticholinergic delirium, and severe hypoglycaemia.

right.title: Preferred safer alternatives
points: Short-acting LOT agents (lorazepam, oxazepam) if needed
